objective: At the owner's request ('Yes, let's continue.', approving PLANAR-THEOREM-20261102-001's recommendation): handles seen from a gluing line. Prove that access at a gluing line depends only on a planar piece around that line, then test on knot spaces with one and two Fano atoms whether new knots appear exactly at gluing lines on handles. No time constraints.
status: Complete 2026-11-03: partially successful. Proved: access is local (plane signed systems with as many lines as odd faces are matching systems with access for every pinning; an intact side of a splice acts as the point or line it replaced; so every pinning by points of a plane piece has access wherever the removal is) and a screening lemma (a one-bit cut reduces creation to a plane knot space). Computed: no creation unless the gluing line lies on a handle or the removal opens a handle attached at a point, which then creates at plane lines out to distance 5; the pinned three-point premise fails on composite spaces (unpinned and four-point new knots). Next: the halo as dimer forcing (2/3)
stop_rule: Stop when locality of access is proved or refuted by a counterexample, and creation is mapped by piece on one- and two-atom spaces, every computation independently checked.
title: Handles seen from a gluing line
